summary: Midday shadow surge causing allocator slow-leak and transient GPU shortages
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated throughput drops and transient 5xxs from their dedicated pool during midday usage window. Behavior started 2026-03-10 ~13:05 UTC and recurred in short waves.

Impact: DataSilo Analytics observed increased P50/P95/P99 latencies for generation routes and a spike in inference failures (5xx/ALLOC_TIMEOUT) for ~10-30 minute bursts. Traffic is primarily short streaming requests (~50-200 tokens) which correlate with the incidents. Customer is on a dedicated pool with reserved capacity and reports this is impacting production job SLAs.

Environment: prod us-east-1, dedicated pool ID ds-4a7c, model gpt-large-v1 pinned. Autoscaler configured with min_replicas=2, target_utilization=0.7.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Send concurrent short streaming requests (mix of 10-50 concurrent clients, 1-2 requests/sec each) to the pinned route for ~10 minutes.
2) Observe intermittent 5xxs and rising p99 latency; GPU attach failures in client logs.

Observed logs/metrics:
- allocator.attach_latency.p50/p95 spikes at same time window (dashboard link in comments).
- autoscaler shows no new replica launches during first 2 waves; subsequent waves triggered scale-up but after >90s.
- node exporter shows bursty PCIe and NVLink io wait on a subset of nodes (node-3x and node-7y).
- Serving runtime logs show ALLOC_TIMEOUT and PREFETCH_LOCK warnings.

Initial hypothesis: A 'shadow surge' of many short streams causes fragmentation in allocator slot assignments (slow-leak of slots), prefetch/kv-cache churn, and transient attach timeouts. The autoscaler did not prevent transient shortages because scale-in policy allowed aggressive shrink during off-peak and burst detection latency prevented timely scale-up. No single hardware failure identified; pattern resembles noisy-tenant interference with allocator slow-paths.

Immediate impact mitigation requested: customer asked for rapid action to stop 5xxs and reduce latency spikes. They prefer a short-lived mitigation rather than rolling traffic to another region.

Requested next steps:
- SRE: temporarily increase min_replicas for ds-4a7c pool and pin allocation affinity to reduce slot fragmentation.
- Support: enable debug-level allocator logs for the pool for 2 hours and collect attach/evict traces.
- Eng: evaluate prefetch lease behavior and scale-in thresholds for short-stream workloads.

Attachments: customer logs (uploaded), support traces, dashboard timeseries links (see comments).
comments: 2026-03-10 13:20 UTC - Aisha Kumar (Support): Acknowledged ticket to customer; opened investigation and escalated to SRE. Slack: #support -> #sre. Notified customer that we will apply short-term isolation if needed.
2026-03-10 13:35 UTC - Customer (DataSilo): Confirmed bursts are repeatable on their workload pattern and provided sample client logs showing ALLOC_TIMEOUT errors.

2026-03-10 14:05 UTC - Priya Desai (SRE): Initial triage — telemetry shows attach_latency p95 jump from 120ms -> 900ms during waves; autoscaler attempted scale-up but average provisioning latency ~95s. Suspect allocator slot fragmentation and prefetch eviction thrash on nodes node-3x/node-7y.

2026-03-10 14:40 UTC - Liam O'Connell (Eng): Will enable allocator debug and run a targeted min_replicas bump for the dedicated pool (ds-4a7c) for 2 hours. Also creating a temporary affinity rule to move noisy tenant to a separate pool for isolation. Linked PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4781
2026-03-10 15:10 UTC - Customer: Accepted temporary isolation; requested monitoring and no service restarts during peak window.

2026-03-10 16:05 UTC - Priya Desai (SRE): Temporary mitigations applied: min_replicas set to 4, affinity rule applied to divert bursty streams to isolation pool. Observed immediate reduction in 5xxs; p99 latency down ~40% for affected routes. Collecting debug traces for postmortem.

2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Liam O'Connell (Eng): Collected allocator traces and KV-cache histograms. Found repeated short prefetch lease renewal churn causing >30% increase in allocator state transitions. Drafting follow-up fix to delay aggressive prefetch eviction under short-stream-heavy workloads.

2026-03-12 12:50 UTC - Aisha Kumar (Support): Customer confirmed service restored to normal for the monitored windows. Customer requested a follow-up call next week to review long-term mitigation plan.
investigation_notes: Allocator trace: spike in slot rebinds and a small number of stuck leases (~1-3 per node) that recovered after 60-120s.
Autoscaler: scale-in had pruned pool to 2 replicas ~30 minutes before midday surge; decider delay + provisioning latency meant first scale-up attempt was late relative to surge onset.
Node metrics: node-3x and node-7y show PCIe latency and brief NVLink thrash correlated to attach latency peaks; could be co-tenant IO bursts.
Serving runtime: PREFETCH_LOCK logs precede ALLOC_TIMEOUT by ~6-12s in most traces — suggests prefetch eviction/locking interplay with allocator slow-paths.
Customer-side: client traces show many short-lived connections (stream open -> complete in <2s) which encourages slot churn and small-batch inefficiencies.
resolution:
Short-term mitigation applied 2026-03-10: increased pool min_replicas to 4 during peak window, applied temporary affinity to isolate noisy burst streams to a separate pool, enabled debug allocator logs and collected traces. Impact: immediate reduction in 5xxs and ~40% p99 improvement.

Long-term actions: follow-up engineering ticket to add burst-detection delay to scale-in, adjust prefetch lease eviction policy for short-stream workloads, and improve allocator slot compaction to avoid slow-leak. Postmortem meeting scheduled 2026-03-17.

Status: Customer satisfied with immediate mitigation; changes to runtime scheduled under ENG prioritization.
